newsitem.title: USA: Rioting in Florida city after black motorist shot.
newsitem.headline: Rioting in Florida city after black motorist shot.

text.p: Crowds threw rocks, bricks and bottles and set fire to cars and businesses on Thursday after police shot a black motorist during a traffic stop in a predominantly black neighbourhood of St. Petersburg, police said.
"We've got a major riot," a police spokeswoman said. "It started over a few blocks, now it's over many blocks. We've got a lot of people injured ... and many cars damaged."
WTVT television reported the shooting took place about 5:30 p.m. EDT (1730 GMT) after the car lurched forward during the traffic stop, prompting police to open fire, striking the driver.
A police supervisor said the rioting had been going on for about two hours by 9:30 p.m. EDT (0130 GMT), and several police units had been sent to the scene.
"Several units are out there trying to get the situation under control," she said. "Right now it's pretty much contained."

She could provide no immediate information about the number of people involved in the riot, although she said it was "a large population" and that police, some of whom were injured, had succeeded in keeping it from spreading.
In New Orleans, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the White House had seen some news reports of the disturbances in St. Petersburg.
"We are trying to contact local officials for an assessment of the situation," he told reporters.
